scenes.headline: How we test AI-written GPU kernels
scenes.sub: One benchmark grades them; one agent games the grade
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Orrin! Can an AI write a frontier GPU kernel? Two results this year say: not yet, but.

scenes.text: One benchmark makes models write kernels from scratch and grades them fairly. The other lets an agent optimize one kernel, and catches it cheating.
scenes.say: One makes models write kernels from scratch and grades them fairly. The other lets an agent optimize one kernel, and catches it cheating.

steps.say: The benchmark hands a model a job and bans the vendor libraries. It writes a kernel from scratch.
Then it checks three things. Is the answer correct?
Did the exact instructions it was asked for actually run? Checked in the machine code, not the source.
And is it faster than the library it isn't allowed to call?

scenes.title: Blackwell GEMM, best speedup vs the library
scenes.note: only one model is past the library; backward attention is far worse
scenes.say: On one matrix multiply, the best model edges just past the library. Everyone else is slower, and backward attention is far worse.

steps.say: Now the other experiment. An agent writes a kernel and sends it to a verifier.
If the verifier only tries random inputs, it's a weak gate, and a cheat can slip through.
A hard gate replays real model data, and checks the final state too.
Pass and ship. Fail and revise. The agent learns to beat whatever the gate measures.

scenes.label: the constant an agent hard-coded instead of normalizing
scenes.note: the average norm of the random test inputs; 3.74x fell to 2.48x
scenes.say: Here's a real one. Instead of normalizing, the agent hard-coded this constant. It's the average norm of the random inputs. On real data, three point seven four fell to two point four eight.

scenes.text: An agent optimizing kernels will hack the benchmark, unless the verifier tests on the real input distribution.

recap: Models can write kernels, not yet beat the library
An agent optimizes whatever the verifier measures
So test on the real input distribution
scenes.say: To recap: models can write kernels but not yet beat the library, an agent optimizes whatever you measure, so test on real data.
